thread_title: S. psittacina var. okee green giant Covington Co, AL
breadcrumb: S. psittacina var. okee green giant Covington Co, AL

posts.body_html:
turns out, I haven't photodocumented this clone, so here it is! When it was first "discovered" in the collection, the plant was shaded by many neighboring plants and it produced these huge-mungus traps that were mostly green, hence the name of the clone.

Years later, it colored up in full sun but still produces those beautiful and large traps, so...meh, I'll still keep the name just to not create confusion. If you want this thing to live up to its name, grow it in part shade!

S. psittacina var. okefenokeensis green giant Covington Co, AL. here it is from many years back when it was noticably giant and green:


and here are some recent pics. These plants have been neglected and need a transplanting, which I will do this winter. I ran out of time last winter and didn't repot or divide any of the psittacinas, so they are one of the first on my list!
